🚨 Decision needed — fix before market open

IQV's stop went in wrong. Plan was stop-limit trigger $231.50 / limit $228.50. What's actually live (order 61789563, placed 2026-08-04 00:24 UTC) is a plain STOP at $228 — a market order on trigger, zero gap protection. This is the exact mechanism that turned CAPR's planned -36% stop into an actual -71.9% fill on Jul 27. TP1 sell limit $250 GTC (order 61789562) is correctly in place. Cancel/replace the stop with the stop-limit, and confirm the two orders are OCA-linked so one cancels the other on fill.

One more thing before you resubmit: per news search, Aug 3's intraday low touched $231.22 — a hair below your planned $231.50 trigger. That's a real level, not a typo, but it means the trigger is tight against current chop. Sanity-check it still makes sense before firing the replacement order, or you risk a same-week whipsaw stop-out on noise.

Readings vary 216–230% depending on methodology/source (GuruFocus 229.9% Aug 2 vs. an alternate calc at 215.4% Aug 3) — both land firmly in overvalued territory. Meanwhile forward P/E at 19.6x is actually a touch below its 5-year average, because EPS estimates have been rising faster than prices — the market's paying up on cap-to-GDP terms but not on a pure earnings-multiple basis. Two different overvaluation signals disagreeing is itself useful information.

Implication for you: stretched but not obviously euphoric on earnings terms — keep the stop-limit discipline tight (starting with fixing IQV's today) rather than treating this as a reason to sit out.

Last historical episodes at this level: 2000 dot-com peak, 2021 COVID bubble peak.

Separately, two insiders sold this week: a Form 4 CEO-level sale of ~$26.1M and a Form 144 sale of $1.25M (Eric Sherbet, 19.2% of his position, $249.16 avg, Jul 29) — normal post-breakout profit-taking, not a red flag on its own, but worth tracking if a third sale shows up. 📚 Today you learned

Bookings / Book-to-Bill Ratio (Services & CRO Businesses)

For a services business like IQV, "bookings" — new contract value signed this quarter — matters more than revenue for forward visibility. Revenue is bookings already being worked off; bookings are the pipeline that becomes revenue over the next 12–24 months. IQV just posted record $3.15B in Q2 bookings, ahead of the $4.37B revenue print itself — a book-to-bill ratio above 1.0x, meaning new business is coming in faster than existing backlog is burning down. That's the real reason the guide got raised, not just the beat. In forex you never had this lag between "deal signed" and "cash recognized"; in CRO/consulting/services names, book-to-bill is your leading indicator, the way order flow is for a dealer — a strong quarter with weak bookings is a yellow flag for the next one.

Also today: backlog — the cumulative unworked bookings balance; CROs disclose this explicitly, and its growth rate is the multi-quarter-ahead version of book-to-bill.
